name: Zeus
role: King of the Olympian gods and lord of the sky
fun_fact: Zeus was hidden as a baby in a Cretan cave and fed by the goat Amaltheia, so that his father Cronus could not swallow him.

name: Demeter
role: Olympian goddess of grain, harvest and the fertility of the earth
fun_fact: Her Roman name is Ceres, which is the root of the modern English word cereal.

name: Persephone
role: Queen of the Underworld and goddess of spring growth
fun_fact: She is also called Kore, meaning simply the maiden, and was worshipped under both names in different cults.

name: Hades
role: God of the dead and ruler of the Underworld
fun_fact: The Greeks often avoided his name and called him Plouton, the wealthy one, because his realm held the earth's mineral riches.

name: Prometheus
role: Titan who sided with humanity and stole fire for them
fun_fact: His name means forethought, and his punishment was to be chained to a rock while an eagle ate his liver, which regrew each day.

name: Pandora
role: The first woman, shaped by the gods as part of Zeus's punishment of humanity
fun_fact: Her name means all-gifted, because each god contributed a different quality to her before she was sent to Epimetheus.

name: Perseus
role: Hero who beheaded Medusa and rescued Andromeda
fun_fact: The myths make him the founder of Mycenae, and his descendant Herakles is the greatest of the Greek heroes.

name: Athena
role: Olympian goddess of wisdom, craft and strategic warfare
fun_fact: She was said to have been born from the head of Zeus, fully grown and armed, after he swallowed her mother Metis.

name: Theseus
role: Hero-king of Athens and slayer of the Minotaur
fun_fact: Athenians credited him with bringing the villages of Attica together into one city-state and honoured him as a founder.

name: Odysseus
role: Hero of the Odyssey, known for cunning and endurance
fun_fact: He tried to avoid the Trojan War by pretending to be mad and sowing a field with salt, until his infant son was placed before the plough.
